$description: The visual regression frame set. Each entry is one deterministic rendering of the preview. A frame exists because some axis of it has broken before, or because a contract says it must not break; the 'why' field records which. Captures live in validation/captures/<date>-<topic>/ and are compared with tools/compare-captures.py.
$status: Frame set and comparison tool are complete. The capture driver that walks this file automatically is NOT yet written; frames so far were driven manually through a real browser. See proposals/crystal-2.0-status.md, task 14.

frames.why: The primary composition. Guards the material hierarchy, pill geometry and focus ring.
Dark mode resolves a different Stone fill; regressions here do not show in light.
Control surfaces: dock, segmented, tabs, fields, table.
Caught a real defect: selected controls rendered white-on-white at 1:1 after a specificity change. Four full-effects frames missed it.
The [data-effects=opaque] path carries its own selector weight and can drift from the media-query path.
Forced colours discards box-shadow, so the focus ring must survive as an outline.
Caught a real defect: a Highlight fill put HighlightText on Chromium's Canvas-coloured text backplate, erasing the selected segment's label.
Logical properties must mirror: bubble corners, menu padding, no horizontal overflow.
Motion recipes and their material choreography.
Generated from the component catalogue; guards the table surface and the docs page scaffolding.
Icon grid rendering and the 24px/1.8px stroke contract. The path was wrong until 2026-09-17 and this frame silently guarded a 404 page; the capture driver now refuses a non-OK response.
Narrow layout must not overflow horizontally and must keep 44px targets.
The documentation home, which is now the index page. Guards the side menu, the Frost panel behind it, and the live material specimens on the overview.
Frost and the menu resolve differently in dark; the overview specimens are the only place the three materials appear side by side.
A specification page with a current menu entry. Guards that selection reads by label weight alone and that menu entries stay Plastic rather than inheriting the Resin of .cr-control.
Selection must be a Highlight ring, not a fill. A filled current entry is erased by Chromium's text backplate, which is the defect this rule exists to prevent.
Below 860px the menu collapses behind its toggle. Guards that the toggle is present, reaches 44px, and that the page does not overflow.

The only composition on the site that exercises Haze inside a Resin frame. The rule forbidding Resin inside Resin is audited in the DOM, but the recess that makes the Haze fill read as the frame's content — an inset dark top edge and light bottom edge, under a light source above — is purely visual and was gated by nothing. Clipped to the composition itself: anchored to the page, the frame re-rasterised on every edit to the prose above it, and a baseline that changes for reasons unrelated to what it guards is a baseline nobody reads carefully. The focus ring, actually focused. Every other frame photographs a page where nothing holds focus, so the six-layer recipe had no visual coverage at all — 2.1.0 changed it from four halo layers to six and all eighteen frames passed at zero tolerance.
The feather alphas differ by mode (46/30/17/8 light, 56/38/22/11 dark), so a light-only focus frame guards half the recipe.
Forced colours discards box-shadow, so the ring must survive as an outline. forced-colours-light has claimed to guard exactly this since it was written, with nothing focused in it.

The Resin scrollbar. `.cr-scroll-resin` appears on this site only as escaped sample code, so the live Resin scroller is `.cr-table-scroll`, and it overflows only when the viewport is narrow — at 390px this one scrolls 243px sideways and paints a 12px horizontal bar. Anchored to the heading rather than to an index, because `.cr-table-scroll` matches thirty-two elements on this page and the twenty-third of them is not a thing anybody can keep true. Headless Chromium paints no scrollbar only because Playwright passes --hide-scrollbars; this frame drops it, which is what D-4 recorded as a property of the browser.
The Frost scrollbar. A scrollbar belongs to the material it scrolls, and the two differ by thumb colour, so one frame cannot stand for both.

reblessing.rule: A baseline is re-blessed only when the change to it is intended and explained.
procedure: 1. Capture the new frames and run tools/compare-captures.py against the committed baselines.
2. For every frame that differs, look at both images. A diff you cannot explain is a defect, not a new baseline.
3. Record the reason in the capture directory's README.md next to the before and after images.
4. Commit the replaced baselines and that README in the same commit as the change that caused them.
Never re-bless a baseline in a commit that also changes behaviour elsewhere: the reviewer cannot tell which change moved the pixels.
